articles.title: Deulkkotsoop "Field · Flower · Forest" Café / MTT
articles.summary: The Deulkkotsoop café is situated on a neglected site that already felt complete, and the design team chose to let the architecture quietly belong to the landscape rather than imposing new forms. By integrating the building with the existing terrain, the project preserves the natural character of the area while providing a functional public space. The result is a harmonious blend of architecture and environment that respects the site's history.

articles.title: Jun Matcha Club Cafe / Matter of Something
articles.summary: Jun Matcha Club transforms a former residential garage in Jakarta into a contemplative matcha experience that slows down the pace of the neighborhood. The interior design emphasizes ritual, with spaces dedicated to the preparation and enjoyment of matcha. This adaptive reuse project offers a quiet counterpoint to the area's bustling café scene.

articles.title: Paso Nara / Instituto Superior de Arquitectura y Diseño
articles.summary: The Instituto Superior de Arquitectura y Diseño hosted a new edition of the Taller del Desierto, an intensive workshop that brings together students from multiple design disciplines. Participants collaborated to develop and build a 1:1 scale model, fostering interdisciplinary dialogue. The event highlights the institution’s commitment to experiential, cross‑disciplinary education.

articles.title: Refuge House / Elisa Porto Arquitetura
articles.summary: Located in Foz do Iguaçu’s Atlantic Forest, Refuge House balances architecture, nature, and thermal comfort in a humid subtropical climate. The design employs passive strategies to manage high humidity and hot summers while maintaining a strong connection to the surrounding forest. The result is a climate‑responsive home that harmonizes with its environment.

articles.title: Pavillon Monk / L. McComber
articles.summary: The Old Brewery Mission is constructing a permanent supportive housing pavilion near Monk metro station to address Brazil’s housing crisis. The pavilion will contain eighteen studio apartments designed to provide stability for people experiencing homelessness. This social architecture project demonstrates how public housing can be integrated into urban transit hubs.

articles.title: Beyond the Handmade Aesthetic: Why Craft Needs New Construction Economies
articles.summary: The article argues that the resurgence of handcrafted materials—brick, lime plaster, carved stone, bamboo, and rammed earth—signals a shift toward environmental responsibility and cultural continuity in architecture. It calls for new construction economies that value craft over mass production. The piece highlights how handmade techniques can coexist with modern building practices.

articles.title: Kifisia Apartment: A Reconfiguration of Domestic Boundaries / Georgios Apostolopoulos Architects
articles.summary: The renovation of a 1970s apartment in Kifisia began with the removal of all internal partitions, revealing the building’s structural potential. By exposing the existing framework, the project redefines domestic boundaries and creates a more open, flexible space. The design showcases how subtraction can unlock new spatial possibilities.

articles.title: Tecno Camon 50 Ultra 5G Review: A $420 AI Phone With Built-in Gemini, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Grok
articles.summary: Tecno’s Camon 50 Ultra 5G is a budget smartphone that bundles multiple AI assistants—Gemini, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Grok—into a single device. The phone offers 5G connectivity and a suite of AI‑powered features at a price point of $420. Reviewers note that the device democratizes AI access for everyday users.

articles.title: 5 Tiny Homes That Feel Twice Their Size Thanks to Light and Glass
articles.summary: The article showcases tiny homes that use strategic lighting and glass to create an illusion of spaciousness. Each design incorporates large windows, reflective surfaces, and clever layouts to maximize natural light. These examples demonstrate how thoughtful design can overcome the constraints of small footprints.

articles.title: MVRDV’s Bihailou Turns a Commercial Complex Into a Vertical Neighborhood
articles.summary: MVRDV reimagines a commercial complex in Shenzhen’s Shatoujiao neighborhood as a colorful vertical village. The design blends architecture, public life, and local identity into a three‑dimensional community. The project illustrates how mixed‑use developments can become vibrant social hubs.

articles.title: The Children’s Bed Adults Keep Wishing Came in Their Size
articles.summary: The piece discusses children’s furniture that balances practicality with thematic design, focusing on a particular bed that appeals to both kids and adults. It highlights the challenge of creating functional yet playful pieces for young users. The article showcases how thoughtful ergonomics can broaden a product’s appeal.

articles.title: This Retro Apple IndyCar Livery Looks Like The Perfect Next Step After The Company’s F1 Partnership
articles.summary: The article presents a retro Apple IndyCar livery design that could serve as a natural progression following Apple’s Formula 1 partnership. It examines how the livery blends brand identity with motorsport aesthetics. The design is positioned as a potential next chapter in Apple’s racing ventures.

articles.title: Weber Is Shutting Off the June Oven’s AI Camera, and a $90 Air Fryer Already Does The Same Thing
articles.summary: Weber is discontinuing the AI camera feature in its June Oven, citing cost and complexity. Meanwhile, a $90 air fryer offers comparable AI‑driven cooking assistance at a fraction of the price. The move highlights the growing competition in smart kitchen appliances.

articles.title: The Cleaning Robot That Knows When a Bathroom Needs It
articles.summary: A new cleaning robot uses sensors to detect bathroom usage and initiates cleaning cycles accordingly, improving hygiene in public restrooms. The device integrates AI to optimize cleaning schedules and reduce manual labor. This technology represents a step forward in smart sanitation solutions.

articles.title: This LEGO Phoenix’s Talons Actually Grip the Perch, and It’s Weirdly Convincing
articles.summary: The LEGO Phoenix figure features talons that realistically grip the perch, showcasing impressive engineering within a toy design. The detail adds a level of authenticity that appeals to collectors and children alike. The piece demonstrates how small design choices can enhance playability.

articles.title: Where Sculptural Balconies Meet Mediterranean Light and Coastal Living
articles.summary: The article explores balconies along the Athenian Riviera that function as extensions of domestic life, providing shade, conversation, and sea air. These sculptural spaces blend architectural form with Mediterranean light to create inviting outdoor environments. The design emphasizes the role of balconies in coastal living.

articles.title: Woonpioniers models adjoining Dutch homes on "a game of Tetris"
articles.summary: Dutch studio Woonpioniers designed interlocking houses in Utrecht that create adjoining yet distinct residences within a single gabled volume. The modular approach allows two families to share a plot while maintaining separate identities. The project showcases innovative use of space in urban residential design.

articles.title: Five ice cream shops that provide cool respite from the summer heat
articles.summary: The piece highlights five stylish ice cream shops around the world that offer a cool break during heatwaves. From London to Buenos Aires, each shop combines culinary delight with thoughtful design. The article showcases how hospitality spaces can respond to extreme temperatures.

articles.title: six-tatami garden tea room layers salvaged timber, titanium, and steel in ichihara, japan
articles.summary: The six‑tatami garden tea room in Ichihara layers salvaged timber, titanium, and steel to create a glazed volume that transitions between the tea room and an annex. The design blends traditional materials with contemporary elements to honor Japanese tea culture. The project demonstrates how mixed media can enhance spatial experience.

articles.title: designboom shop drop: material & craft celebration of tactile design objects
articles.summary: The shop drop showcases design objects that emphasize traditional craftsmanship across ceramics, metals, and hardwoods. Each piece highlights the tactile qualities of material and the skill involved in its creation. The event celebrates the enduring relevance of hand‑made design.

articles.title: australian architects ditch the traditional box in favor of climate-responsive home designs
articles.summary: Australian architects are rethinking domestic design to adapt to hotter climates by bending walls and employing climate‑responsive strategies. The projects showcase innovative approaches to passive cooling and natural ventilation. This shift reflects a broader move toward sustainable, climate‑smart architecture.

articles.title: material, structure, and scent converge in so koizumi’s south korean solo exhibition
articles.summary: The exhibition merges Koizumi’s visual work with a scent‑based environment, exploring the interplay of material, structure, and olfactory experience. Visitors encounter installations that engage multiple senses, creating an immersive narrative. The show highlights the potential of interdisciplinary art practices.

articles.title: To the Red Dot Newsroom
articles.summary: The article announces the opening of the Red Dot Design Award newsroom, a dedicated space for media coverage and public engagement. It outlines the newsroom’s role in showcasing award winners and providing resources for journalists. The initiative aims to strengthen communication between the award and its audience.

articles.title: General press information on the Red Dot Design Award
articles.summary: This piece provides comprehensive press information about the Red Dot Design Award, including submission guidelines, award categories, and past winners. It serves as a reference for journalists and designers seeking details about the competition. The article supports transparency and accessibility for the award’s stakeholders.

articles.title: CIGA design EDGE Collection | IN DEPTH - Time+Tide Watches
articles.summary: The in‑depth feature explores CIGA’s EDGE Collection of Time+Tide watches, highlighting the brand’s design philosophy and technical innovations. It examines how the watches combine luxury aesthetics with functional performance. The article positions the collection as a benchmark in contemporary watch design.

articles.title: The Outline: Duolingo update, a V&A Lego set, and the white stuff – 17/09/26 - designweek.co.uk
articles.summary: The article covers recent updates from Duolingo, a new V&A Lego set, and other design news items. It provides a snapshot of current trends in educational technology, toy design, and broader industry developments. The piece serves as a quick briefing for design professionals.

articles.title: Ypsomed Receives The Red Dot Design Award 2026 For YpsoLoop - Clinical Leader
articles.summary: Ypsomed’s YpsoLoop clinical leader product has been awarded the Red Dot Design Award 2026, recognizing its innovative design and user‑friendly features. The award highlights the device’s contribution to medical technology and patient care. This accolade positions Ypsomed as a leader in medical device design.

articles.title: Depth by Aleksei Kipin Wins Iron in A' Software Design Awards - The National Law Review
articles.summary: Depth, a software design by Aleksei Kipin, secured the Iron award at the A' Software Design Awards. The recognition underscores the project’s excellence in user experience and interface design. The award highlights the growing importance of software aesthetics in the design community.
